sentences.text: Judge (POCSO), Morigaon in POCSO Case No. 62/2024, under Sections 366/376(3) of the IPC read with Section 4 of the POCSO Act, whereby the prayer of the petitioner to recall PW-1 for further cross-examination was rejected.

The learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioner was facing trial from custody and, therefore, proper instructions could not be given to the defence counsel at the relevant time.
As a result, the cross- examination of PW-1 could not be conducted to the satisfaction of the petitioner, thereby compromising his defence.

The learned counsel for the petitioner has further drawn the attention of this Court to Petition No.
3651/2025 dated 03.12.2025, wherein the petitioner had indicated certain specific questions proposed to be put to the alleged victim/PW-1 in order to strengthen his defence.

In support of his submissions, the learned counsel for the petitioner has relied upon the judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Natasha Singh vs. CBI (State), decided on 08.05.2013 in Criminal Appeal No. 709 of 2013; Rajaram Prasad Yadav vs. State of Bihar; Vijay Kumar vs. State of Uttar Pradesh; and Rajeshwar Prasad Misra vs. State of West Bengal, amongst others.
The learned counsel for the petitioner has further submitted that allowing the recall of the victim for further cross-examination on limited questions would not jeopardize the trial in any manner nor would it cause any inconvenience to PW-1.

sentences.text: The learned APP for the State, however, has submitted that the provisions Page No.# 3/3 of the POCSO Act, more specifically Sections 33(5) and 33(6), discourage the repeated recalling of a child witness for the purpose of testifying before the Court, in order to ensure that the child is not subjected to unnecessary hardship during the course of the trial.

In response, the learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the present case is not one involving repeated recall of the witness, but rather a request for a single opportunity to conduct further cross-examination on limited questions, as indicated in Petition No. 3651/2025.

Upon going through the materials on record and after hearing the learned counsel for the parties,
this Court is of the opinion that the petitioner may be granted one opportunity to put the questions in further cross-examination, as projected in Petition No. 3651/2025.

For the said purpose, the learned Trial Court shall fix a particular date for the appearance of PW-1 before it, subject to payment of such cost as may be determined by the learned Trial Court to be paid to PW-1 for attending the proceedings on that particular date.

It is made clear that upon the appearance of PW-1, the petitioner shall be granted the opportunity to cross-examine the witness, and the same shall be restricted only to the questions indicated in Petition No. 3651/2025.

The learned Trial Court shall further ensure that the cross-examination is conducted on the date so fixed and shall also ensure that there is no repeated recalling of the witness for any further Ajijur Rahman Alias Ajijul Ali Alias ... vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32708327/
